findings.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — [P3, confidence 100, wrong-shape/invariant] The pipeline validates the raw `LokiQuery` with verbatim `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))`, so `expr: '$optional'` can resolve to `''` after validation and is still partitioned and dispatched as an empty query in both splitters; centralizing interpolation-then-validation in one prepared-target boundary passes the deletion test by removing the duplicated pipelines and decouples callers, and although filtering first saves interpolation for already-empty inputs, that micro-optimization cannot preserve the post-transform non-empty invariant.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 — [P3, confidence 100, coupling/unbounded-work] The shard entry applies verbatim `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` and then delegates every shard group to `runSplitQuery`, whose line 299 applies the same transformation again, making one target incur five applications in the checked-in test and scaling redundant preparation with shard-group fanout; splitting a single prepare-once boundary from an internal prepared-query executor passes the deletion test, and although the current replacement may usually be cheap and idempotent, `applyTemplateVariables` is an API hook allowed to add filters or reshape a query and carries no idempotence contract, so the ownership defect survives that counterargument.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — [P3, confidence 100] The changed pipeline executes verbatim `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` and adds no acceptance case where a nonempty raw variable expression resolves to `''`, so that target survives preprocessing and is dispatched as a meaningless empty query in both time- and shard-splitting flows; the strongest counterargument is that empty variable values are uncommon, but optional dashboard selections legitimately produce them, so the unhandled edge survives.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:75 — [P2, confidence 100] The sole new test uses verbatim `expr: 'count_over_time({a="b"}[$__auto])'` but never covers the adjacent documented invariant that `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` must keep `$__range` queries unsplit after interpolation was moved ahead of classification, so a regression can split such a query against per-chunk ranges and change its result; the strongest counterargument is that the current helper may leave `$__range` untouched, but the change explicitly broadens preprocessing of `expr` and no test fixes that contract.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84 — [P2, confidence 75] The new shard regression request omits `filters` while production now passes verbatim `request.filters` at shard entry and then delegates each generated request to `runSplitQuery`, leaving no acceptance proof that user ad hoc filters are applied exactly once rather than dropped or duplicated across the nested preprocessing path; the strongest counterargument is that `applyTemplateVariables` may currently be idempotent for filters, but the test stubs only `replace` and even expects five applications, so it cannot establish that behavior.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:299 — [P2, confidence 100, duplicate transformation / latent fragility] The new verbatim `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` prepares each target before `datasource.runQuery` reaches `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, which applies the same hook again (and the shard wrapper adds a third pass), so a valid ad-hoc label value such as literal `$region` is first inserted into LogQL, then expanded as a dashboard variable while the original filter is appended again, producing contradictory matchers and silently empty results across every split request; although ordinary variable values make replacement look idempotent and identical duplicated predicates are logically harmless, `$` is legal label data and `applyTemplateVariables` has no idempotence contract, so the failure appears as soon as a replacement output itself resembles a template token and is amplified by shard fanout.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.test.ts:76 — [P2, confidence 100] Spec-coverage gap: the sole non-sharded regression fixture is verbatim `createRequest([{ expr: 'count_over_time({a="b"}[$__auto])', refId: 'A', step: '$step' }])`, so first-target-only interpolation still passes while a second active target retains `$__auto` or `$step` and is partitioned or sent incorrectly; the strongest counterargument is that production currently uses `.map(...)`, but the gap survives because this test cannot distinguish that contract from an implementation that applies the helper only to index zero.

public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 — [P3, confidence 100] Fragile test structure: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` couples the interpolation check to four mock shard groups plus the wrapper pass, so a harmless regrouping or removal of redundant interpolation fails despite every dispatched query remaining correct; the strongest counterargument is that an exact count can catch skipped preprocessing, but it does not survive because the observable `runQuery` targets are the actual contract and five calls are incidental execution topology.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — [P3, confidence 100, wrong-shape/invariant] The pipeline validates the raw `LokiQuery` with verbatim `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))`, so `expr: '$optional'` can resolve to `''` after validation and is still partitioned and dispatched as an empty query in both splitters; centralizing interpolation-then-validation in one prepared-target boundary passes the deletion test by removing the duplicated pipelines and decouples callers, and although filtering first saves interpolation for already-empty inputs, that micro-optimization cannot preserve the post-transform non-empty invariant.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the code filters for non-empty `query.expr` BEFORE applying template variable interpolation. This means a query with `expr: '$someVar'` would pass the filter (since '$someVar' is truthy), but after `applyTemplateVariables` is called, if the variable resolves to an empty string, the query would still be processed. The diff shows the pipeline order: `.filter((query) => query.expr).map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))` in both querySplitting.ts and shardQuerySplitting.ts. This is a real logical bug where post-interpolation empty expressions could be dispatched.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that runShardSplitQuery delegates to runSplitQuery which applies applyTemplateVariables again. However, examining the diff, runShardSplitQuery calls splitQueriesByStreamShard (line 54), not runSplitQuery. The diff shows two separate functions: runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts and runShardSplitQuery in shardQuerySplitting.ts. There's no evidence in the diff that splitQueriesByStreamShard calls runSplitQuery or applies applyTemplateVariables again. The finding misreads the code structure and makes an incorrect claim about double application of template variables.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/plugins/datasource/loki/querySplitting.ts:298 — [P3, confidence 100] The changed pipeline executes verbatim `.filter((query) => query.expr)` before `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters))` and adds no acceptance case where a nonempty raw variable expression resolves to `''`, so that target survives preprocessing and is dispatched as a meaningless empty query in both time- and shard-splitting flows; the strongest counterargument is that empty variable values are uncommon, but optional dashboard selections legitimately produce them, so the unhandled edge survives.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff changes the order of operations: `.filter((query) => query.expr)` now runs BEFORE `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...))`. This means if a query has `expr: '$variable'` where `$variable` is non-empty, it passes the filter. But after template variable interpolation, if `$variable` resolves to an empty string `''`, the query would still be processed. The tests added only verify that variables like `$__auto` and `$step` are replaced with non-empty values ('5m'), but don't test the edge case where a variable resolves to empty string. This is a legitimate edge case bug - dashboard variables can legitimately be empty/unselected, and this would result in empty queries being dispatched.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the test at line 109 uses `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` which couples the test to the internal implementation detail of how many times `applyTemplateVariables` is called (5 times for 5 shards). This is a legitimate test design concern - the test is fragile because changes to shard grouping logic would break this assertion even if the actual query interpolation behavior remains correct.
